absence-context-diagnostic.scope: fixed context-length and punctuation-contributor comparison on consumed public fixture; no production gap decision

absence-lookback-diagnostic.scope: fixed end-anchored lookback and punctuation-contributor comparison on consumed public fixture; no production gap decision

absence-beam-diagnostic.scope: beam-search decoding comparison at unchanged acceptance gates on consumed public fixture; no production gap decision

absence-native-conversion-diagnostic.scope: production-native PCM conversion comparison on consumed public fixture; no production gap decision

criteria.conversion: production native equal-channel average and FIR resampling; bounded offline packet input

conclusions: Ignoring punctuation improves the original inserted-dialogue reliable runs from 4/2/2 to 4/5/4 words, still below six.
Extending fixed starts forward to 12/15 seconds adds context but does not pass inserted-dialogue gates. End-anchored lookback at 12/15 seconds also fails.
Five-beam decoding retains only 2/3/3 reliable words in inserted dialogue and rejects two outputs with native status 4. The production greedy decoder is retained.

Using the production native equal-channel average/FIR converter gives inserted-dialogue reliable runs of 4/3/2; one quiet output is rejected with status 4. This also fails the unchanged six-word criterion.
Earlier offline FFmpeg mono resampling is not byte-equivalent to the actual native conversion; its results are development observations, not active-player proof.
initialIncompleteRuns: The first beam diagnostic stopped on an assertion after four completed inserted windows. A complete fixed-matrix rerun records every rejected native output; it is not a successful recognition retry.

The first native-converter diagnostic stopped after ten windows. The fixed matrix was repeated with rejection recording; clipping counts are unavailable from the native converter and are not inferred as zero.
